chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Harun ibn al-Jahm, from Hafs ibn Umar, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Measure your food, for indeed the blessing is in the measured food.'
ai.seo_question: Why is measuring food important in Islamic tradition?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) links the Prophet’s instruction to measure food with the presence of barakah, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on precision in trade to prevent gharar (uncertainty). This practice not only ensures fairness in transactions but also serves as a spiritual discipline, transforming mundane acts into sources of divine blessing.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Haroun Bin Al Jahm, from Hafs Bin Umar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Measure out your foodstuffs, for the Blessings are in the measured foodstuffs’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bandar has narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from his father Harun ibn al-Jahm from Hafs ibn ‘Umar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘
Measure your food; blessings come with measured food.’”
